extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models as embodied brain for robotic manipulation, covering 5 dimensions (Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis), 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.publisher: State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Institute for Brain and Intelligence, Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.rai:dataCollection: RoboBench combines data from large-scale real-world robotic datasets and in-house collection. The benchmark constructs datasets across diverse embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid robot), attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation. Data are drawn from open-source robotic datasets and enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets (Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, RDT-1B, LIBERO, and others) with curated in-house collection. Representative frames are sampled from high-quality robotic videos for planning tasks. Perception data uses real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static attributes, and human-labeled bounding boxes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit instructions are rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Natural language step descriptions are mapped to predefined function sequences using LLM-based conversion.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. Frame sequences are extracted from robotic videos as standardized inputs. Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), which are refined by human annotators. All perception data are standardized into multiple-choice QA format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generates structured annotations for planning tasks including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata, which are refined by human annotators. Each step is mapped into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists. For perception tasks, Gemini performs video segmentation for temporal grounding, combined with manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes. Execution-level failures are labeled by experts. For affordance prediction, representative frames are sampled and annotated with three types: static (contact points), dynamic (motion trajectories), and mobile (base positions). 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for video segmentation, structured annotation generation, and temporal grounding), GPT (for generating functional properties and distractors, rewriting explicit instructions into implicit forms)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current benchmarks emphasize execution success or suffer from incomplete dimensions and limited task realism. Existing planning evaluation methods have drawbacks: text-similarity metrics only measure surface-level linguistic similarity, multiple-choice evaluations deviate from real-world open-ended tasks, and LLM-based judgments introduce subjectivity and inconsistency.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is designed for evaluating MLLMs as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. The benchmark systematically evaluates five dimensions: Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis. It provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
